thread.title: Apple ‘Has Never Been Better,’ Tim Cook Tells Jim Cramer

title: Apple ‘Has Never Been Better,’ Tim Cook Tells Jim Cramer
text: Apple ‘Has Never Been Better,’ Tim Cook Tells Jim Cramer More Apple ‘Has Never Been Better,’ Tim Cook Tells Jim Cramer## AppleToday, Apple (AAPL) stock closed with nearly 1.9% gains at $150.79. The stock remained volatile as many Wall Street analysts expressed their views on the company. Plus, the ongoing US–China trade talks, which entered their third day, remained in investors’ focus. The S&P 500 Index (SPY), NASDAQ Composite Index, and Dow Jones rose 1.0%, 1.1, and 1.1%, respectively.## Tim Cook talked to Jim CramerEarlier today, CNBC’s Jim Cramer interviewed Apple’s CEO Tim Cook. During the interview, Cook spoke about many key factors affecting Apple’s business lately as well as criticism.Denying any possibility of consistent fundamental weakness, Cook said, “We think about the long term. And so when I look at the long-term health of the company, it has never been better. The product pipeline has never been better. The ecosystem has never been stronger. The services are on a tear.”While expressing his views about the recent steep drop in Apple shares, Cook noted that “I’m never surprised by the market, to be honest with you, because I think the market is quite emotional in the short term.”On January 3, Apple stock fell by 10% after Apple cut its first-quarter guidance, mainly citing Chinese iPhone sales weakness.Before Cook’s comments today, Bernstein analyst Toni Sacconaghi said on CNBC, “No need to rush buying Apple today.” Sacconaghi suggested that Apple isn’t inexpensive based on its relative valuation.Today, other tech companies Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG), Facebook (FB), Intel (INTC), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Netflix (NFLX) rose 1.7%, 0.7%, 0.7%, 3.3%, 0.6%, 0.9%, and 1.6%, respectively. At the same time, NVIDIA (NVDA) and Qualcomm (QCOM) were down 2.5% and 0.9%, respectively.Chinese companies Alibaba (BABA) and Baidu (BIDU) rose 2.6% and 0.5%, respectively, today.
